Subject: RFP - traffic mirroring evidence and threshold validation

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of AstraCloud's RFP evaluation we need a focused deliverable that shows how Redwood handles 'mirror' traffic and how you validate thresholds and degradation modes. Specifically we need: 1) a short, reproducible test plan we can run or watch (lab schedule); 2) artifacts showing latency/throughput at mirror ratios (1:1, 1:5, 1:20) and during burst windows; 3) the exact pass/fail criteria you use for threshold breaches (tail quantiles, error budgets, retry/backoff behavior).

Can you provide a plan and any CSVs or runbooks that show the expected artifacts? We would like a live demo or recorded run on your side the week of July 26 if possible. Omar from Benchmark Labs is available to observe.

Thanks,
Priya Desai
Director, Platform Engineering
AstraCloud Inc.

Hi Priya —

Appreciate the clarity. We can deliver exactly that. High-level proposal:

- Quick pre-read (attached): configuration file for traffic mirror harness and a short runbook.
- Lab sessions: two focused runs (dry-run + full-bake) on July 27 and July 29 (PST) — 45 minutes each with 30 min for Q&A. Omar welcome.
- Artifacts we will hand over: CSV latency timelines, per-quantile breakdown (p50/p90/p95/p99/p999), request error inject logs, and the traffic mirror config used to generate the experiment.
- Acceptance criteria: explicit thresholds we will test against (see below). If you agree we will produce the attachments and a short recording of the July 27 run.

Proposed threshold checks (we will provide measured numbers in the artifact):
- Steady-state: p95 latency degradation <= 1.5x baseline at mirror ratio 1:5
- Burst window (30s spike): p99 latency stays below 2.5x baseline and system error rate < 0.5%
- Fallback: when capacity saturation occurs, autonomous fanout fallback to a smaller model variant must trigger within 8s and maintain <5% user-level error increase.

I'll loop marissa and karthik to produce the runbook and artifacts. Will also attach the traffic-mirror-config.yml as a starting point.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: RFP - traffic mirroring evidence and threshold validation (artifacts and method)

Jordan / team —

Attaching the core artifacts and a short method summary. Attachments: traffic-mirror-config.yml (stub), latency-threshold-report.csv (sample rows), runbook-traffic-mirroring.pdf (step sequence). Key pieces below:

1) Environment baseline
- Model: rdx-base-3B (fp16), single-shard on A100-40GB equivalent
- Serving runtime: Redwood v2.4 with KV caching and continuous batching enabled
- Baseline profile: 20 concurrent sessions, mean prompt length 60 tokens, baseline p95 = 120ms

2) Traffic mirroring approach
- Mirror ratio is applied at the ingress gateway: for mirror=1:5, 1 out of 5 live requests are forked to the mirror harness and counted but not returned to the client. Mirror traffic goes through same runtime path (no sampling) to capture realistic kernel selection and cache effects.
- Mirror tagging: traffic includes identical headers and a mirror flag; mirror responses are logged to a separate sink.

3) Test matrix (short form)
- Mirror ratios: 1:1, 1:5, 1:20
- Throughput sweep: from 50 RPS up to 1.5x peak expected for 10 minutes, with 30s microbursts (5x RPS) injected at minute 3 and minute 7.
- Duration: 30 minute runs per matrix cell for steady-state, 10 minute microburst-only short runs

4) Metrics we collect
- Latency: p50/p90/p95/p99/p999 and latency time-series per second
- Resource: GPU utilization, queue depth, kernel runtime distribution
- Errors: timeout, OOM, internal-retry, model-fallback events
- Observability: span-level traces with sampling for tail analysis

5) Pass/fail logic (automation in runbook)
- If p99 during steady-state > 3x baseline, mark as degradation and capture sample traces
- If error rate > 1% sustained for >60s, fail the cell and trigger fallback scenario
- If model fallback time > 8s repeatedly, record as operational risk and include mitigation note

6) Artifacts included (what you'll receive)
- CSVs: per-second latency timeline and quantile rollups (latency-threshold-report.csv)
- Config: traffic-mirror-config.yml (filters, mirror ratios, seed traffic generator)
- Runbook PDF: exact sequence, commands, infra snapshot hashes and expected output locations

Notes: we intentionally mirror full request/response to capture KV cache cold/warm dynamics. For compliance, mirrored payloads are redacted in the CSVs; raw traces can be shared under an NDA.

Let me know if Astra wants a different baseline model variant or if Omar wants to run a tuned batch that matches their production prompt distribution.

-marissa
Marissa Cole
Technical Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Thanks — this is exactly the level we were hoping for. A couple quick clarifications before the runs:

- For the p95 <= 1.5x baseline check, does baseline mean the same workload when *not* mirrored, or the baseline you measured previously with empty mirror (i.e., mirror disabled)?
- On fallback timing: can you confirm which signal triggers the automatic fallback (latency queue depth threshold, error rate, or a combined signal)? We need the precise metric so our SREs can map to their alarm rules.

If those two items are explicit in the runbook we can sign-off on observers and confirm Omar's attendance. We prefer the July 27 morning slot (09:00 PST).

Regards,
Priya

Subject: Re: RFP - traffic mirroring evidence and threshold validation (confirmations)

Priya —

Short answers:
- Baseline definition: baseline = mirror disabled (identical traffic profile, same model config). In our artifacts we'll include a baseline run and the mirrored run so you can compute the degradation ratio directly.
- Fallback signal: primary trigger is queue-depth cross-section (requests queued > 450ms for more than 4s) combined with a spike in internal retry rate (>= 0.8% over 30s). We use the combined rule to avoid noisy single-metric flips; the runbook includes the exact PromQL rules and thresholds (see runbook-traffic-mirroring.pdf).

We will schedule the live run on July 27 at 09:00 PST and will record. Artifacts and CSVs will be posted to the shared Drive link within 3 hours of the run. If you want Omar to run a parallel client from BenchLabs, we will accept a signed NDA (link below) to share raw trace payloads.
